Subject: Inference health & term opportunity — LumaHealth

Caroline — great speaking last week. I pulled the usage and performance snapshots and wanted to summarize where we see a near-term opportunity to both stabilize latency and move you from ad-hoc hosted calls to a predictable reserved model that lowers unit cost. Highlights from our side (Q2 -> Aug):

- Token trajectory: 18M tokens/month average in Q2 rising to ~26M in July (+45%).
- Latency: median generation time for your default model profile is ~220ms, p95 at 1.1s during morning peak (12–2pm PT).
- Cost: current hosted spend is trending toward a monthly variability of +/- 28% driven by burst events.

Proposed near-term motion:
1) Pilot a small Dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalent) for 60 days to reduce p95 and stabilize costs.
2) If pilot meets latency SLO (p95 < 700ms) and 15% CPI reduction, roll into a 12→24 month term with stepped discounts and burst credits.
3) Share an ROI recap and a lightweight SOW for procurement.

Next steps I suggest: we send an ops snapshot and ROI recap to your procurement team and schedule a 30-min tech handshake with our infra lead. Attached is a preliminary per-model usage export so your engineers can validate assumptions.

Attachments: luma_usage_breakdown_aug.csv (csv)

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks for the write-up and the CSV. Quick clarifications from our side before we loop in procurement:

1) Can you break out cost impact by model family (small vs large) and include the amount attributable to embeddings vs chat tokens?
2) We need an apples-to-apples latency comparison for our production traffic (we run a lot of short-turnaround inference for triage flows). Your p95 target looks promising but we need more concrete numbers per endpoint.
3) Who would own key rotation and KMS during a pilot in a VPC?

I'll copy Andrew (CFO) after we have a short ROI recap that shows expected monthly savings at 20/30/40% uplift. If you can include an outline of the procurement path (PO terms, invoicing cadence, standard SOW), that will speed things up.

—Caroline

Caroline — thanks, good questions. See answers inline and attached ROI recap.

1) Cost breakout: attached CSV includes per-model token mix and a separate tab for embeddings vs chat. In short, ~62% of tokens are generation calls, 28% embeddings, 10% rerank — moving the generation-heavy endpoints to Dedicated reduces unit token cost by our estimate of 18–26% (model-size dependent).
2) Latency by endpoint: we ran a production-seeded replay of your short-turnaround triage endpoints (attached). For the pilot config (2x reserve), expected med/p95: 160ms / 640ms. Our runtime will also enable prefix caching for repeated context which should lower tail latencies in practice.
3) KMS: during a VPC pilot, you retain key ownership; we support Bring-Your-Own-KMS. We'll document the steps in the SOW.

Attached: rdw_roi-recap-202709.pdf (PDF) — short ROI table with savings scenarios and step discount model. Also linking a draft SOW and DocuSign template below.

Suggested mutual action plan (MAP):
- Week 0: Sign mutual NDA amendment for pilot (procurement) and confirm PO contact.
- Week 1: Execute pilot SOW, set up VPC peering / KMS handoff.
- Week 2–5: Pilot run (observability live, ops playbook). Weekly sync.
- Week 6: Performance readout + commitment decision. If go, apply term conversion and credits per SOW.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/r/abcd1234
Drive: https://redwood.cr/drive/rdw-LUMA-usage-report

Ben
